thread:
Alex Chen: Hey team — we're getting an escalated ticket from a customer hitting a sustained 429/503 pattern after a deploy. They say latency spikes briefly, then a flood of 429s for ~45s, then recovery. Account: acct_9a2f, region: us-west-2. Can someone triage?
Priya Patel: Do we have the request ids or sample headers? 429 storms often mean client-side fanout + missing Retry-After honor.
Alex Chen: Attached logs from their app (pasted):
```
resp 429 {"error":"rate_limited"} headers: x-rate-limit-remaining: 0 x-rate-limit-reset: 1678439205 x-request-id: r-0a1b2c
resp 429 {"error":"rate_limited"} headers: x-rate-limit-remaining: 0 x-rate-limit-reset: 1678439205 x-request-id: r-0a1b3d
```
Jordan Reyes: Interesting that reset timestamp is identical across many requests — implies a shared token bucket on our side hit zero. Does the customer use parallel clients or one client with many threads?
Alex Chen: They say they have a short-lived burst test: a fleet of Lambda workers that all retry on 5xx/429 with SDK default retry strategy.
Luca Marino: Which SDK and version? Some older SDKs do immediate retries without jitter which can create retry storms.
Alex Chen: They are on node-sdk v1.3.0 (our legacy defaults).
Priya Patel: That rings a bell. v1.3.0 default: maxRetries=4, backoff base=100ms, exponential with small jitter. There's a bug where jitter wasn't full-randomized. If many clients retry at same backoff intervals, you get synchronized bursts.
Jordan Reyes: Can we confirm our service's behavior? Ops Oncall, any autoscaler activity or sudden pool shrink at that time?
Ops Oncall: I pulled infra logs for acct_9a2f window: no node drains, GPU pool steady. Throughput limit hit on routing: per-customer token bucket exhausted for ~52s, then tokens refilled. No autoscale events.
Alex Chen: Customer says they also saw some 401s intermittently right after 429s — could be auth retries (stale token) or our auth service rate‑limit.
Priya Patel: Two separate issues possible: 1) client retry backoff pattern causing burst that exhausts the shared quota; 2) client not using idempotency keys for POSTs so retries cause duplicate state/side-effects.
Luca Marino: Reproduction steps we gave them:
1) spawn 200 concurrent clients hitting chat.generate with short prompt for 10s
2) have the client SDK retry on 429/5xx with defaults
3) observe initial latency bump then 429 flood
We should ask them to try: set maxRetries=2, enable full jitter, and respect `Retry-After` / `x-rate-limit-reset` headers.
Alex Chen: They sent a repro script. Paste of their node snippet (simplified):
```js
for (let i=0;i<200;i++) {
  client.generate({prompt: 'hi'}).catch(err => { /* retry */ });
}
```
No idempotency header. No backoff library.
Jordan Reyes: Action items:
- Priya: confirm SDK default changes and publish guidance for v1.x users (we should recommend full jitter and honoring Retry-After).
- Luca: verify server returns `Retry-After` consistently and edge cases where we return `x-rate-limit-reset` but no Retry-After.
- Ops: confirm per-customer burst bucket size and whether we should surface a warning when sustained near-zero remaining.
- Alex: provide the customer mitigation steps and a small patch snippet they can apply client-side.
Priya Patel: Draft SDK guidance: set `maxRetries=3`, use exponential backoff with full jitter (rand(0, base * 2^attempt)), obey `Retry-After` header if present, and include idempotency-key for non-idempotent endpoints. Also consider client-side leaky bucket to smooth bursts.
Luca Marino: On server side: we return both `x-rate-limit-remaining` and `x-rate-limit-reset` for token buckets. `Retry-After` is only set on certain 429 paths (legacy quota enforcer). I'll open a ticket to unify so clients can always rely on `Retry-After` seconds when we reject due to quota.
Ops Oncall: We can add an alert for "per-customer token bucket <= 10% for >30s" to warn support before customers escalate.
Jordan Reyes: Customer-facing mitigation note to send: 1) temporarily throttle their concurrency to 20 workers; 2) patch SDK retries to full jitter and lower maxRetries; 3) add idempotency keys for create calls; 4) ask us to enable a temporary higher burst bucket for acct_9a2f while they ramp.
Alex Chen: I drafted the reply, sending now.
SupportBot: Escalation created: INC-2026-4021, assigned to eng-runtime and infra.
Priya Patel: Follow-up: we should also publish an FAQ entry about "retry storms" with recommended client configs and a sample leaky-bucket wrapper for node/python SDKs. I'll start a doc. :memo:
Luca Marino: For longer-term: evaluate per-route adaptive throttling by request cost, and surface `x-client-retry-hint` to tell polite clients to back off in seconds.
Jordan Reyes: Good. Also note: encourage customers to run a low-signal repro that uses our SDK built-in rate limiter (we have one in v2) instead of rolling custom naive retries.
Alex Chen: Thanks all — I'll close once customer confirms they're OK with the temporary burst increase and client patch.
Priya Patel: I'll include suggested sample code in the reply (full jitter example + idempotency header).
Luca Marino: I'll file the internal ticket to unify Retry-After headers (infra-612).
SupportBot: Incident INC-2026-4021 updated by Priya Patel: added SDK guidance attachment.
